units.text: INT. VICTORIAN OBSERVATORY - NIGHT (1887)
A copper dome open to the stars.
A great brass telescope on a creaking mount, its tube pointing at a smear of the Milky Way.
Chalk equations cover a slate board.
A YOUNG WOMAN in a plain gray dress (20s) stands at the eyepiece, a notebook clutched to her chest.
She has slipped in through the coal door.
Behind her, from the stairwell, a lantern rises.
An old man, PROFESSOR EUSTACE PEMBERTON (70s, nightshirt, dressing gown, white whiskers), emerges, glaring.
Who is there? Show yourself!
units.name: PROFESSOR

units.text: She spins, notebook falling.
He lifts the lantern.
The light finds her face.
Professor, please. I only wished to see.
units.name: YOUNG WOMAN

units.text: This is a private instrument.
units.name: PROFESSOR

units.text: I am Ottoline Marsh, sir. I wrote to you eleven times.
units.name: YOUNG WOMAN

units.text: He lowers the lantern a little.
His beard trembles.
The scullery girl's cousin? The one who counts comets?
units.name: PROFESSOR

units.text: I do not count them, sir. I find them.
units.name: OTTOLINE

units.text: He stares at her.
Then at the telescope.
Then at the sky through the open dome.
Show me.
units.name: PROFESSOR

units.text: She hesitates, steps to the eyepiece, adjusts a brass knob with practiced fingers.
He peers in after her.
A long silence.
God in heaven.
units.name: PROFESSOR

units.text: Yes, sir.
units.name: OTTOLINE
